plan.title: Intro to Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG)
plan.analogy: Like going to a library (or a neighbour) to fetch the exact page you need before writing an answer, instead of trying to remember everything yourself.
plan.running_example: A student asks: “What are the latest COVID‑19 guidelines for schools in Delhi?” The system looks up a government circular PDF, a recent news article, and the school’s own policy document, then uses that info to answer.

sections.title: Before We Start
sections.goal: Know what you will learn and why it helps an AI career
points: You will see how computers find up‑to‑date facts before answering
Helps build AI tools that are reliable and trustworthy

sections.title: What Is RAG?
sections.goal: Understand the basic idea in plain words
points: RAG means Retrieval‑Augmented Generation – first fetch relevant text, then let a language model write the answer
Analogy: like reading a book chapter before answering a question

sections.title: Why Does It Matter?
sections.goal: See the problem RAG solves and its benefits
points: LLMs stop at the knowledge they were trained on – they can be old or miss private data
RAG gives fresh, private, and source‑backed answers without retraining the model

sections.title: How Does It Work?
sections.goal: Learn the two main phases with a running example
points: Indexing phase: split each document into small chunks, turn each chunk into a numeric vector (embedding), store vectors in a vector database
Query phase: turn the user question into a vector, find the most similar chunks, attach those chunks to the prompt, let the LLM generate the final answer
